units.retained: fraction of 20 C value, tested at temperature

conventions.retained_long_vs_short: Design heated aluminium molds on the long_10000h row: a mold held at temperature 8 h/day reaches 10,000 h in ~5 years. short_0p5h is only for first heat-up checks.
conventions.max_service_C: full_strength = design with the 20 C numbers less <=5-10%; derated = usable with the long-term retained fraction; never_above = overaging/softening/embrittlement risk.
conventions.cost_index: per kg relative to 6061-T651 = 1.0 (~US$8/kg distributor cut plate, 2025-26); order-of-magnitude only - get quotes.
conventions.machinability: aa_rating = Aluminum Association-style A-E letter (approx); index_1212 = AISI basis 1212=100 (steels, annealed or as noted); rel_mrr_vs_P20 = rough metal removal rate vs P20 pre-hard on a typical VMC with carbide (aluminium is usually spindle-limited).
conventions.confidence: published | derived | estimate - estimates must be shown to the user as such.
conventions.use: page lists: plate, insert, backing, stop; [] = not offered on the page (2024 ages and changes size above ~120 C)

mold_materials.name: 6061-T6 / T651 rolled plate

retained.notes: Long-term values from ASM/Kaufman typical properties after 10,000 h at temperature (24 C 310/276; 100 C 290/262; 149 C 234/214; 204 C 131/103; 260 C 51/34 MPa UTS/YS), interpolated to 150/200/250 C. MMPDS data: 100 h at 150 C gives no loss, so loss develops between ~100 h and 10,000 h. Short-time row approximate (MMPDS-style 1/2 h curves).

fatigue_MPa.basis: Engineers Edge fit S = 14479/sqrt(N) + 96.5 MPa (R=-1, smooth); lower than MMPDS-approx 185/130/105 - verify before release

mold_materials.typical_use: General cavity plates, cores, lids, backing plates for PU/epoxy/resin molds; the default aluminium choice. At 150 C design to 0.78 x yield (long-term).
sources: ASM Handbook Vol 2; Kaufman, Properties of Aluminum Alloys (ASM 1999)
LIGO T1000564 (MMPDS citation, 150 C/100 h no loss)

mold_materials.name: 7075-T651 rolled plate

retained.notes: ASM/Kaufman after 10,000 h: 24 C 572/503; 100 C 483/448; 149 C 214/186; 204 C 110/87; 260 C 76/62 MPa. Strength collapses by overaging above ~120 C. Short-time row: Lin et al. 2020 (CJME) flow stress at 0.2% strain 536/408/305/198 MPa at 25/130/180/230 C.

fatigue_MPa.basis: R=-1 smooth; 5e8 value 159 MPa (ASM/MatWeb); others read from S-N curves (approx)

mold_materials.typical_use: High-pressure cavity/core plates and thin ribs for LOW temperature work only (RTV, PU, epoxy <= 100 C). Do not use for rubber or hot-cure resin (>= 130 C).

mold_materials.name: MIC-6 cast tool & jig plate (Alcoa/Arconic, now Howmet/Kaiser distributors)

retained.notes: ESTIMATE. No published elevated-temperature curve found; already stress-relieved and low strength, so it is dimensionally stable but has little strength to lose. Treat as estimate until supplier data is obtained.

fatigue_MPa.basis: ESTIMATE ~0.33 x UTS at 1e7 (typical for cast aluminium)

mold_materials.typical_use: Flat, stable backing plates, heater/thermal plates, lids and fixture plates where flatness (0.015 in max) and +/-0.005 in thickness matter more than strength. Low thread strength: tapped holes need inserts or through-bolts.

mold_materials.name: 2024-T351 plate

retained.notes: ASM 2024-T3 after 10,000 h (approx 24 C 483/345; 100 C ~455/330; 149 C 379/310; 204 C 186/138; 260 C 76/62 MPa). mold_materials.name: 5083-O / H116 plate, or cast 5083 tooling plate
mold_materials.spec: ASTM B209 / B928; EN AW-5083; cast tooling plates (e.g. Alpase M-1, ACP 5080, ALCA PLUS)

retained.notes: ASM 5083-O after 10,000 h (24 C 290/145; 100 C 275/145; 149 C 215/130; 204 C 150/115; 260 C 115/75 MPa). Non-heat-treatable, so no overaging: the most stable aluminium here. H116 strain-hardening anneals out progressively above ~150 C. Sensitization (beta phase) above 65 C makes it prone to intergranular/stress corrosion if wet.

mold_materials.typical_use: Large, light, stable platens and lid frames at higher temperatures where strength needs are low; weldable. Cast 5083 tooling plate is a flat, stress-free alternative to MIC-6.

fasteners_common.inch_spec: ASTM A574 alloy-steel SHCS (ASME B18.3 dimensions). Proof stress 140 ksi (<=1/2 in), 135 ksi (>1/2 in); min UTS 180/170 ksi.
fasteners_common.preload_rule: Fi = 0.75 x proof load (Fastenal/Unbrako practice for re-usable joints). For steel bolts in hot aluminium start lower, see thermal_preload.
fasteners_common.torque_formula: T = K * d * Fi, K = 0.15 lubricated (oil/anti-seize), 0.16 as-received black oxide, 0.20 dry. Torque is an indirect measure: +/-25% preload scatter.
fasteners_common.head_bearing: Allowable surface pressure under the head is ~UTS of the clamped material (VDI 2230 Table A9 values are roughly 0.9-1.2 x Rm). 12.9 SHCS at 75% proof put ~400-700 MPa under the head (see head_bearing_pressure_at_preload_MPa) - above 6061 (310 MPa, ~230 hot) and far above MIC-6 (166). Use through-hardened washers (ASTM F436 / ISO 7089-300HV or DIN 6340) or SHCS with larger heads, or reduce preload, on ALL aluminium clamped faces.

thread_engagement.formula: Le/D >= 0.5 * Su_bolt / Su_parent (min 1.0). Derived: internal-thread shear area/length ~2.25 D, parent shear strength 0.6 Su, As ~0.57 D^2, 1.2 margin so the bolt breaks before the tapped thread strips. Use Su_parent at operating temperature (long-term).

thermal_preload.formula: dF = (alpha_clamped - alpha_bolt) * dT * L_grip / (L_grip/(E_b*A_b) + L_grip/(E_c*A_c_eq))  [N]; A_c_eq = VDI 2230 equivalent clamped-cone area (~3-5 x bolt As for typical plates). Also include E(T) for both parts. Heating ADDS preload when the clamped part expands more (aluminium); cooling below assembly temperature removes it.

examples.case: M10 12.9, 50 mm grip, 6061 plates, 20->150 C (E_Al at 150 C)
M10 12.9, 50 mm grip, P20 plates, 20->150 C

consequences: 12.9 SHCS torqued to 75% proof in 6061 reaches ~100% of proof load at 150 C - near yield. Torque aluminium joints to ~60-65% proof, or use a reduced-shank / long-grip bolt (lower kb), or spacer sleeves.
Aluminium under the head and in the threads then creeps/relaxes at 150 C, so preload drops over the first few cycles: re-torque hot after the first 2-3 heat cycles and specify hardened washers.
Steel clamping steel (P20) changes little (~5% of preload).

fasteners_common.washer_rule: Hardened washers on every aluminium clamped face. A hardened washer does not fit a standard SHCS counterbore: counterbore = washer OD + 0.5 mm (critique E2).

when_to_use: Tapped hole in aluminium where the screw is removed often (lids, clamp bars, cavity inserts changed for maintenance): aluminium threads wear and gall.
Required L_e/D for a direct tapped thread exceeds what the plate thickness allows (see thread_engagement).
Any preloaded thread in MIC-6, 5083-O or cast plate (UTS < ~300 MPa), and any aluminium thread that runs hot (>= 150 C) for long periods.
Hot runner / heated-platen contact points and dowel/bolt-down locations in 7xxx mold plate (Arconic QC-10 guidance: hardened steel inserts/bushings at all such contacts).

helical_wire_free_running.brands: Heli-Coil (Stanley Engineered Fastening), Recoil, Bollhoff HELICOIL Plus; ASME B18.29.1 (inch), NASM/MS21209, DIN 8140 (metric)
helical_wire_free_running.material: 304 stainless wire (standard), Inconel X-750 for >430 C
helical_wire_free_running.lengths: 1.0D, 1.5D, 2.0D, 2.5D, 3.0D nominal; use 2.0D in aluminium for structural joints
helical_wire_free_running.needs: STI tap (not a standard tap); tap depth = insert length + ~1/4 turn + tap chamfer
helical_wire_free_running.effect: Parent-material shear diameter rises from D to ~D + 1.3 P (about 1.2 D for 1/2-13); spreads load more evenly; stainless wire stops galling
helical_wire_free_running.drill_note: Drill sizes vary by maker and hole tolerance class; the tool must read the chosen maker's table. Values above: Heli-Coil inch catalog practice / DIN 8140 range; Albany County Fasteners chart (2025) gives Q for 5/16-18, Y for 3/8-16, 17/32 for 1/2-13.

fit_rules: Each located pair of parts: ONE round dowel (press in one part, slip in the other) + ONE diamond/relieved pin or a slot oriented radially from the round pin. Never two tight round dowels across a hot aluminium/steel joint.
Dowel holes depth: ~1.5-2.0 D in each part; through holes or a pull-out thread (tapped dowels) on blind holes so they can be extracted.
Press in the plate that stays put, slip in the plate that comes apart. Slip-fit L/D >= 1.0 for repeatability.

steel_pin_in_aluminium_temperature_effec.formula: loss of interference (diametral) = (alpha_Al - alpha_steel) * dT * d
steel_pin_in_aluminium_temperature_effec.rule: Loss is ~0.0016 mm per mm of diameter at 20->150 C (~0.0016 in/in). A standard light press fit (0.005-0.02 mm) of a 10 mm pin in aluminium is gone by ~80-120 C. Either (a) build in interference >= loss (the press_hole_aluminium_150C columns give ~0.0016 x d + the pin's own m6/+0.0002 in allowance; contact pressure ~90 MPa, von Mises ~150 MPa in the aluminium at 20 C - fine for 6061/7075/QC-10, NOT for MIC-6/5083-O) - install by shrink fit (heat plate to 150-180 C or chill pin), because pressing a hardened pin into aluminium at that interference shaves and galls the bore, (b) shrink-fit by heating the plate to 150-180 C, (c) use a steel bushing that is retained by flange+screws or a high-temperature retaining compound (Loctite 620 rated to 230 C; 638/648 to ~175-180 C), or (d) treat the pin as a slip fit and capture it.

guide_pins_and_bushings.products: Leader/guide pins and bushings: DME, Progressive Components, HASCO Z00/Z10, Misumi GPA/GBA, Meusburger E1000
guide_pins_and_bushings.fit: pin g6/h6, bushing bore H7: running clearance ~0.01-0.04 mm diametral at assembly temperature
guide_pins_and_bushings.count_and_layout: 4 pins for lids larger than ~250 mm; one offset (or one different diameter) so the lid only goes on one way; pins long enough to engage >= 1 D before any cavity/core contact.

thermal_mismatch.formula: mismatch between pin centres = L * |alpha_1 * dT_1 - alpha_2 * dT_2|  (L = distance from the datum pin, or half the pin spacing if centred)
thermal_mismatch.example_same_material: Both halves 6061 at the same temperature: no mismatch. A 10 K difference between lid and base at L = 200 mm: 200 * 23.6e-6 * 10 = 0.047 mm -> more than the 0.01-0.04 mm running clearance; lid binds.
thermal_mismatch.example_mixed: Steel lid on 6061 base, both 20->150 C, L = 200 mm: 200 * (23.6-12.7)e-6 * 130 = 0.28 mm. Do NOT mix lid/base materials with round pins.
thermal_mismatch.recommendation: Use round pin + radially-slotted (or diamond) bushing so growth is free along the line to the datum; add tapered/side interlocks (2-5 deg, hardened, ~0.01-0.02 mm preload at temperature) for final cavity-to-core registration; size guide clearance for the worst plate-to-plate temperature difference the heated platens allow (typically 5-15 K).

guide_pins_and_bushings.bushing_in_aluminium: Hardened steel or bronze bushings in all aluminium guide bores (aluminium galls against steel pins). Press with ~0.002 x d interference for 150 C service, or flange-and-screw retained.

6061_T651_plate.notes: Rolled plate is supplied OVER nominal (ANSI H35.2 / EN 485-4 tolerances, roughly +0.5-3% on thick plate); plan to skim both faces: finished thickness ~ nominal - 0.03 to 0.06 in (0.8-1.5 mm). Above 6-8 in buy 6061-T6 forged block or switch to Alumold/QC-10. Metric plate in Europe is often 6082-T651 (similar properties).

mic6_cast_plate.notes: Sold to finished decimal thickness +/-0.005 in (+/-0.13 mm), both faces machined, flatness ~0.015 in max; no skim needed. Common stock to 2.5 in (Speedy Metals), thicker by order. Metric column is generic cast tooling plate (5083-type ALCA/ACP/Alpase), +/-0.1 mm typical.

7075_T651_plate.notes: T651 to ~4-6 in; thicker sections T7351/T7451 (lower strength, better stress-corrosion). Over-nominal like 6061.

qc10_alumold500.inch: 1-24 (QC-10); 1-8 rolled, 10-27 forged (Alumold 500; Alro stocks to 20 in), sawn to order
qc10_alumold500.notes: Mold-block alloys sold cut-to-size; buy finished-size + ~0.06-0.12 in per face.

p20_prehard.notes: Distributor sawn plate/blocks, any size to ~24 in / 600 mm; supplied rough (+0.06-0.125 in over) with decarb, so allow ~1.5-3 mm per face. Standard mold-base plates (DME inch A/B plates 0.875, 1.375, 1.875, 2.375, 2.875, 3.375, 3.875 in...; HASCO K-plates 22, 27, 36, 46, 56, 66, 76, 96, 116, 136, 156, 196 mm) come finish-ground and are often the cheapest P20 for a standard footprint - verify against catalogs.

sources: Speedy Metals cast plate list / tolerance
McMaster-Carr MIC6 and cast plate tables
DME and HASCO mold-base catalogs (plate series - verify)
